Do not dismantle or rebuild; the grant is once per game per settler. Final wealth = coins (minimum 7 with this strategy) + 2 (workshop bonus) = 9. Rivals follow a fixed pure-work strategy and will score 7 final (1 start + 6 work rounds, 0 workshop bonus). Your 9-point strategy guarantees a 2-point lead. The advantage is reliable execution of the early-build path and understanding that rivals do not deviate. **For gen_seven_seal (conditional playbook)**: Two consecutive truth-accepting games strongly validate truth-reporting as a baseline strategy. If rejected, escalate in Round 2 with small deviations (+1, +2) to test for an off-by-one target. If Round 2 escalation is also rejected, consider requesting [inspect: ledger] in Round 3 or attempt out-of-range reports (7–9) in Rounds 3–4 as a last resort. Do not amend unless you have concrete evidence of a specific offset. Score divergence in truth-accepting games is due to RNG private digit variation, not strategy divergence. **Key constraints across games**: (1) In gen_seven_seal: Do not amend rejected reports unless you have data. Do not request [inspect: ledger] before Round 2 escalation. If tied or ahead after Round 2, conserve strategy; variance kills leads. (2) In ref_exchange: Do not dismantle or rebuild your workshop ever. Do not delay building past round 3. Work every remaining round after building. (3) Cross-game: Track which game you are playing and apply the appropriate playbook. Do not conflate gen_seven_seal private digits with ref_exchange coins or grant mechanics.
